summary: I surveyed 28 curated collections: awesome lists, plugin databases, galleries, chart-taxonomy sites and dashboard templates. Each was verified from shallow git clones, with category counts taken from the raw READMEs, versions and licenses from npm/jsDelivr, and stars from shields.io. The best catalog seed is hal9ai/awesome-dataviz (formerly fasouto, then javierluraschi; CC BY 4.0, last commit 2026-10-13, 4.4k stars). It has about 420 entries in 24 sections, and its JS part (about 133 entries) has a Financial charts section and already lists the 2025-26 newcomers (Flint, Vela, ChartGPU, mapcn, the perspective-dev org). For the gallery taxonomy, use the FT Visual Vocabulary: 72 chart types in 9 relationship categories, in a machine-readable chartTypes.csv (MIT for the software; FT branding is excluded). Use data-to-viz as a second filter: 6 data-shape roots leading to about 39 charts, plus 12 caveats. Data Viz Catalogue (60 methods) and Datavizproject (166 types) are copyrighted, so use them only to check completeness. For reference code, the Apache ECharts examples are the strongest gallery: 377 2D plus 59 GL examples, Apache-2.0, with machine-readable category and 'since' tags. ECharts 6 adds features that suit finance work: axis breaks for intraday gaps and a matrix coordinate system for sparklines and mini-bars inside tables. Vega-Lite has 203 gallery examples (BSD-3) and Plotly has 12 gallery sections. The official Leaflet plugin DB has 578 plugins in 36 categories with frontmatter metadata. 568 are flagged compatible with v1 and none with v2, so pin Leaflet 1.9.4. Use chartjs/awesome as the Chart.js plugin matrix, but its version badges are out of date: chartjs-chart-financial 0.2.1 actually works with chart.js ^4 per npm. The catalogs also exposed traps. ApexCharts is under a dual Community/Commercial license from 5.1.0 (current 8.2.0), which rules it out for a bank, and Tabler's demos still use ApexCharts 7. MapLibre 6.x is ESM-only (the last UMD build is 5.24.0). WASM libraries (Perspective, Vizzu, Mosaic) fail under file://. The AntV cloud-rendering skill and MCP server send data off the machine. AdminLTE 4.10 is license-clean (Chart.js 4.5.1, jsvectormap, Tabulator; all MIT), while Tabler should be used only for CSS and icons. shadcn charts (70 Recharts 3.8 blocks) and Tremor Raw/Blocks are React-only design references. For Step 2, study Microsoft Flint (one MIT spec that compiles to Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly or Excel, with an MCP server) and AntV's SKILL.md packs, Infographic and GPT-Vis (MIT; UMD builds available). My concrete recommendation is a catalog.json keyed by FT category and data shape, linked to ECharts, Vega-Lite and Plotly example ids, which can also serve as the tool manifest the future LLM reads.

libraries.name: awesome-dataviz (hal9ai; ex fasouto/javierluraschi)
libraries.capabilities: About 420 entries in 24 sections. JS: Charting 35, Graph libs 18, Financial charts 9, Maps 22, React 18, Misc 23. Also Dashboards and BI 13, Python 64, Catalogs 11. Mirror site awesomedataviz.com lists 365 tools with stars, commits and license columns.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (catalog)
libraries.reason: The most current and complete library catalog (updated daily in Oct 2026) and the seed for our candidate list. Its Financial and Maps sections are directly relevant. Attribute it if we reuse its text (CC BY).

libraries.name: awesome-d3 (wbkd)
libraries.capabilities: 145 entries: Charts 62, Maps 18, Utils 29, Misc 14, Server 2, plus 20 bl.ocks profiles (dead links). Good source for d3fc, d3-annotation, d3-legend, crossfilter/dc.js, venn.js and d3-composite-projections.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (catalog)
libraries.reason: Stale since 2023 and many plugins target d3 v3/v4. Mine it for a few annotation and legend utilities only.

libraries.name: awesome-echarts (ecomfe)
libraries.capabilities: About 52 entries: Extensions (wordcloud, liquidfill, leaflet/openlayers/maptalks bindings, graph-modularity), framework wrappers, language bindings (pyecharts and 4 other Python libs) and tools.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (catalog)
libraries.reason: Thin and slow-moving, and its makeapie.com community-gallery link is dead. The ECharts examples repo is the better resource.

libraries.name: Leaflet Plugins DB (docs/_plugins)
libraries.license: BSD-2-Clause (repo); each plugin has its own license
libraries.capabilities: 578 plugin .md files in 36 categories, e.g. markers-renderers 80, dataviz 21, clustering 13, heatmaps 8, legends in user-interface. Each file has YAML frontmatter with compatible-v1/v2 flags.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Leaflet 1.9.4 dist/leaflet.js (UMD, 144 KB); most plugins are plain scripts
libraries.reason: The authoritative map-plugin catalog and machine-readable. 568 plugins are flagged v1-compatible and none v2, so pin Leaflet 1.9.4. Key plugins: markercluster, DonutCluster, leaflet-dataclassification, choropleth, Canvas-Flowmap, PixiOverlay, glify.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Plugins add choropleth colour classes, proportional/graduated symbol size, donut clusters showing category shares, flow width and colour, heat density and shape markers.
libraries.interactions_animation: Cluster spiderfy/zoom animation, PixiOverlay WebGL animation, velocity flow animation

libraries.name: chartjs/awesome
libraries.capabilities: 75 table rows with a Chart.js v2/v3/v4 support matrix: chart types (financial, geo, matrix, sankey, treemap, boxplot, error-bars, venn, wordcloud, pcp), plugins (zoom, annotation, datalabels, a11y-legend, chart2music, streaming) and date adapters.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Most plugins ship UMD/min files, e.g. chartjs-plugin-zoom.min.js, chartjs-chart-geo build/index.umd.min.js, chartjs-chart-financial.min.js
libraries.reason: The best plugin map for a Chart.js track. The badges are stale (financial 0.2.1 actually peers chart.js ^4), so verify peerDependencies on npm.

libraries.name: awesome-geojson (tmcw)
libraries.capabilities: 123 entries: operations 27, editors 17, validation 8, services 7, conversion 35, data 19, serialization 6, resources 4. Covers turf, geojson-rewind, simplify and topojson.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (catalog); @turf/turf 7.4.0 turf.min.js UMD
libraries.reason: Useful for picking GeoJSON preprocessing for the Python builder and JS (winding order, simplification, topojson).

libraries.name: awesome-maplibre / awesome-vector-tiles
libraries.capabilities: awesome-maplibre has 236 entries (UI plugins 30, rendering plugins 25, layer types 16, ECharts bindings); awesome-vector-tiles has 142 (servers 40, clients 25).
libraries.offline_classic_script: MapLibre 6.x is ESM-only. The last UMD build is maplibre-gl@5.24.0 dist/maplibre-gl.js
libraries.reason: Only needed if we ship offline vector basemaps. MapLibre 6 breaks file:// classic scripts.

libraries.name: awesome-javascript (Data Visualization section)
libraries.capabilities: 46 entries in DataViz, many from the jQuery era (rickshaw, morris, envision, g.raphael). The Spreadsheet, Table/Grid and Animations sections are more useful. AntV Infographic was added recently.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: Low signal-to-noise for viz and about 40% unmaintained. Use only its grid and animation sections.

libraries.name: awesome-react-components / awesome-vue (chart, map, grid, admin sections)
libraries.capabilities: React: about 23 chart, 11 editable-grid, 12 table and 7 map components. Vue: 9 chart, 8 map, 5 graph and 18 admin templates (vue-data-ui has 60+ components).
libraries.offline_classic_script: No; framework components need a build step
libraries.reason: Framework-bound, so useful only as design inspiration. Several entries are commercial (AG Grid Enterprise, Handsontable, ZingChart, ApexCharts).

libraries.name: awesome-charting (zingchart)
libraries.capabilities: 62 entries: Commercial 8, OSS 27, framework-specific 19, resources 7. The real name is awesome-charting; zingchart/awesome-charts does not exist.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: Stale since 2021 and vendor-biased.

libraries.name: FT Visual Vocabulary (chart-doctor + ft-interactive/visual-vocabulary)
libraries.license: MIT (software only; FT content and branding are copyright)
libraries.capabilities: 72 chart types in 9 categories: Deviation 4, Correlation 5, Change over Time 12, Ranking 8, Distribution 8, Part-to-whole 11, Magnitude 12, Spatial 8, Flow 4. chartTypes.csv is machine-readable and 42 types have D3 v4 templates (58 folders).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Templates use a local d3.min.js (v4)
libraries.reason: The primary navigation taxonomy for our gallery, already familiar to finance audiences. Gotcha: the CSV uses CR line endings. Do not reuse FT styling.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Its taxonomy explicitly covers proportional symbol, bubble, choropleth, cartograms and flow maps.

libraries.name: data-to-viz.com (holtzy/data_to_viz)
libraries.capabilities: A decision tree with 6 roots (Numeric, Categoric, Num&Cat, Maps, Network, Time series) leading to about 39 chart pages, plus 12 featured caveats, about 20 data-format stories and named example CSVs such as 1_OneNum and 18_ListGPSCoordinatesWithValue.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (R/HTML site)
libraries.reason: Gives the second gallery filter (what data shape you have) and a naming scheme for test fixtures. The caveats feed the kit's linting and tips.

libraries.name: D3 Graph Gallery (holtzy)
libraries.capabilities: 47 chart-family pages and 165 small example HTMLs (barplot 14, line 10, bubblemap 6, choropleth, hexbin map, connection map, sankey, chord...).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Examples load d3.v4.js (183 references) or d3.v6.js (126) from d3js.org; they must be ported to the vendored d3 7.9.0 dist/d3.min.js
libraries.reason: Readable minimal D3 snippets, but on old D3 versions and fetched from a CDN.

libraries.name: Apache ECharts examples gallery
libraries.capabilities: 377 2D examples (bar 46, line 40, scatter 36, map 25, matrix 14, candlestick 10, calendar 9, sankey 7, treemap 7...) and 59 GL examples. Metadata is machine-readable (id, title, titleCN, category, since). 28 examples need v6: axis breaks, intraday breaks, matrix sparklines and mini-bars, chord, jitter.
libraries.offline_classic_script: echarts dist/echarts.min.js (UMD, 1096 KB); echarts-gl dist/echarts-gl.min.js (625 KB)
libraries.reason: The best source of license-compatible reference implementations, and auto-joinable to our catalog ids. The v6 features (breaks, matrix) map directly onto pitchbook needs.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: visualMap maps colour, size and opacity; symbolSize callbacks; geo plus effectScatter; polar and radial coordinates; matrix coordinates
libraries.interactions_animation: dataZoom, brush, roam, universalTransition morphs, timeline animation

libraries.name: Vega-Lite examples gallery
libraries.capabilities: 203 gallery items: Single-View 115, Composite 7, Layered 19, Multi-View 18, Maps 12, Interactive 32. The repo has 633 spec files.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. build/vega.min.js (509 KB), vega-lite.min.js (252 KB) and vega-embed.min.js (59 KB) are all UMD
libraries.reason: A grammar-level reference for brushing, linking and annotation layers. Disable vega-embed's online-editor actions in client output.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Full channel set: x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, row/column facets, theta/radius
libraries.interactions_animation: Selections (point/interval), cross-filter and bind inputs; limited animation

libraries.name: Plotly.js gallery
libraries.capabilities: 12 sections, including Financial (waterfall, indicators, candlestick, funnel, time series with range selector), Maps (MapLibre tile maps, choropleth, bubble) and custom controls (dropdown, slider, lasso, range slider).
libraries.offline_classic_script: plotly.min.js UMD, but 4.7 MB
libraries.reason: Good finance and interaction patterns, but the bundle is heavy. Partial bundles are possible if adopted.

libraries.name: Data Viz Catalogue / Data Viz Project
libraries.capabilities: Catalogue: 60 methods in 16 functions, including Kagi, Point and Figure, Span, OHLC, Marimekko and Nightingale rose. Datavizproject (Ferdio): 166 types across 4 facets (Family, Input, Function, Shape).
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a
libraries.reason: Use as completeness checklists only; do not copy text or thumbnails.

libraries.name: shadcn/ui charts
libraries.capabilities: 70 copy-paste chart blocks: area 10, bar 10, line 10, pie 11, radar 14, radial 6, tooltip 9. Uses CSS-variable palettes (--chart-1..5).
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (React/Recharts, build step)
libraries.reason: A modern visual-polish reference (tooltips, gradients, radial KPIs) to re-implement in our ECharts/Chart.js theme.

libraries.name: Tremor Raw / Tremor Blocks
libraries.capabilities: About 35 components: AreaChart, BarChart, BarList, CategoryBar, ComboChart, DonutChart, SparkChart, Tracker, ProgressCircle. Blocks: 300+ dashboard sections (381 .tsx files).
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (React + Recharts 2.15)
libraries.reason: Its KPI-primitive vocabulary (BarList, CategoryBar, Tracker) is worth borrowing. The project was acquired by Vercel in Jan 2025 and the npm package is frozen.

libraries.name: Tabler (@tabler/core + @tabler/icons)
libraries.capabilities: Bootstrap-based dashboard UI with 139 Astro preview pages (dashboards, datagrid, charts, vector maps) and 5k+ MIT SVG icons.
libraries.offline_classic_script: dist/js/tabler.min.js (132 KB) plus CSS; icons as SVG/sprite
libraries.reason: Good for layout and icons, but 23 demo pages use ApexCharts 7.0.0 (dual license). Strip it and swap in ECharts/Chart.js.

libraries.name: AdminLTE 4
libraries.capabilities: Bootstrap 5.3.8 admin template with Chart.js 4.5.1, jsvectormap 1.7.0, Tabulator 6.6.1, FullCalendar 7.1.1, bootstrap-icons and accessibility docs.
libraries.offline_classic_script: dist/js/adminlte.min.js (27 KB); demo pages load deps from cdn.jsdelivr.net, so they must be vendored
libraries.reason: The license-clean dashboard reference (all MIT dependencies). Its look is generic, so restyle it to pitchbook standard.

libraries.name: ApexCharts
libraries.license: ApexCharts License: dual Community (<US$2M revenue) / Commercial, from 5.1.0. Last MIT was 5.0.0
libraries.capabilities: Full SVG chart suite. Premium tiers gate Trellis, Linked Views and similar features.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes (UMD), but irrelevant given the license
libraries.reason: License change in July 2025: an investment bank is above the US$2M threshold. Many lists and templates (Tabler, vue-apexcharts) still present it as free.

libraries.name: MapLibre GL JS
libraries.capabilities: WebGL vector-tile maps with 3D terrain and data-driven styling
libraries.offline_classic_script: Only up to 5.24.0: dist/maplibre-gl.js (1032 KB, plus CSP variants). 6.x ships only .mjs and worker .mjs
libraries.reason: Pin 5.24.0 if vector maps are required. Offline glyph, sprite and tile packaging is non-trivial, so Leaflet 1.9.4 with GeoJSON is the default.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Data-driven expressions for circle-radius, colour, extrusion height and heatmap

libraries.name: Microsoft Flint (flint-chart)
libraries.capabilities: An AI-oriented chart spec with 70+ semantic field types. One spec compiles to Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly or editable Excel charts. flint-chart-mcp is an MCP server.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No; ESM only (dist/index.js, per-backend dist folders). It would need pre-bundling to IIFE
libraries.reason: Its channel vocabulary (x, y, color, size, shape, radius, lat/lon, OHLC, angle) is a strong template for our own JSON spec and for the Step-2 local-LLM interface.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Explicit channels: color, opacity, size, shape, strokeDash, radius, angle, row/column, latitude/longitude, OHLC

libraries.name: AntV Infographic / GPT-Vis / chart-visualization-skills
libraries.capabilities: An LLM-friendly infographic DSL (streaming-tolerant, about 200 templates per a secondary source). GPT-Vis is a markdown-like chart syntax. The skills repo has 9 SKILL.md agent skills (G2, G6, X6, Infographic, GPT-Vis, T8).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: infographic dist/infographic.min.js (UMD, 857 KB, global AntVInfographic); gpt-vis dist/umd/index.min.js
libraries.reason: A direct reference for Step 2 (importing skills, LLM output to visuals). The chart-visualization skill and mcp-server-chart render via the AntV cloud API, so data would leave the machine; use only the local renderers.

libraries.name: Vela (LuxAlgo)
libraries.capabilities: Financial charting with a headless core, native WebGL2 renderer and plugin SDK
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/vela.global.min.js (IIFE, 1019 KB)
libraries.reason: A promising permissive alternative to TradingView Lightweight Charts, which has an attribution clause. Still pre-1.0, so watch it.

libraries.name: ChartGPU
libraries.capabilities: WebGPU charting for very large and streaming series
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (ESM; 135 MB unpacked)
libraries.reason: WebGPU dependency, 0.x maturity and package size do not fit offline client reports.

libraries.name: Perspective (now perspective-dev org)
libraries.capabilities: Streaming pivot grid with charts, WASM query engine, user-defined expressions
libraries.offline_classic_script: dist/cdn/*.js exists, but it fetches a .wasm file, which fails under file://
libraries.reason: Its 'client types their own formula and queries' UX is ideal, but WASM loading breaks double-click delivery without inlining tricks.
libraries.interactions_animation: Pivot, filter, sort, expression columns, live updates

key_insights: Gallery navigation: use FT Visual Vocabulary's 9 categories as the primary axis and data-to-viz data shapes as the secondary filter. Fill finance gaps (OHLC, Kagi, Point and Figure, Marimekko, Span, Fan) from the Data Viz Catalogue. Store it as catalog.json, which can also be the tool manifest for the Step-2 LLM.

ECharts examples metadata (src/data/chart-list-data.js: id, title, titleCN, category[], since) can be joined automatically to our catalog ids, giving a license-compatible (Apache-2.0) reference implementation per chart type.

ECharts 6 finance features: axis breaks (bar-breaks-*, intraday-breaks-* for trading-hour gaps) and the matrix coordinate system (sparklines and mini-bars inside a grid, think-cell style). 28 examples require 6.0.0.

Leaflet plugin DB frontmatter: 568 of 578 plugins flagged v1-compatible and none v2, so pin Leaflet 1.9.4. Thematic stack: markercluster plus DonutCluster (category shares), leaflet-dataclassification (classes, graduated symbols, auto legend), choropleth, Canvas-Flowmap, PixiOverlay or glify for scale.

License trap: ApexCharts is dual-licensed (Community only under US$2M revenue) from 5.1.0 (2025-07-09); current 8.2.0. Tabler's preview pages still use ApexCharts 7.0.0, so strip it. AdminLTE 4.10 uses Chart.js and is clean.

file:// trap: MapLibre GL JS 6.x ships only .mjs (the last UMD is 5.24.0), and Leaflet 2.0 is alpha and ESM-first. WASM libraries (Perspective, Vizzu, Mosaic/DuckDB-WASM) need fetch of .wasm. Flint, Unovis and TanStack core are ESM-only and must be pre-bundled to IIFE in our build.
List badges go stale: chartjs/awesome shows chartjs-chart-financial unsupported on v4, but npm 0.2.1 peers chart.js ^4.0.0. Always verify with npm view <pkg> peerDependencies.
Example code age: D3 Graph Gallery uses d3 v4 (183 references) and v6 (126); FT visual-vocabulary templates are d3 v4. Budget porting to the vendored d3 7.9.0 dist/d3.min.js.
FT chartTypes.csv has old-Mac CR line endings (wc -l returns 0). Parse with Python's csv module and newline=''.

Content licenses: awesome-dataviz is CC BY 4.0 (attribution needed if text is reused); awesome-d3, awesome-echarts, awesome-geojson and awesome-react-components are CC0; Data Viz Catalogue and Datavizproject are copyrighted with no license; the FT MIT license excludes FT branding.

Lightweight Charts (TradingView) is Apache-2.0 plus a condition to show an attribution notice and a tradingview.com link on the user-facing page. The NOTICE file is in the GitHub repo, not the npm tarball.

Online-only parts hidden in the lists: Google Charts loader, ECharts gmap/amap/bmap extensions, vega-embed's 'Open in Vega Editor' action, and the AntV chart-visualization skill and mcp-server-chart (cloud rendering). Exclude all of them for confidential client data.

KPI primitive vocabulary from Tremor Raw: BarList, CategoryBar, Tracker, SparkChart, ProgressCircle. Visual polish from shadcn charts: CSS-variable --chart-1..5 palettes, indicator tooltips, radial KPIs. Re-implement in vanilla JS with ECharts/Chart.js.

Python parallels for the builder: pyecharts 2.1.0 (ECharts option JSON), altair 6.3.0 (Vega-Lite JSON) and folium 0.20.0 (Leaflet) prove the split where Python emits a spec and JS renders it. They inject CDN links by default, so our builder must own the vendor/ asset paths.

Repo renames to track: awesome-dataviz (fasouto, then javierluraschi, now hal9ai; same commit), zingchart's list is awesome-charting not awesome-charts, Perspective moved from @finos to @perspective-dev, and Tremor's npm package is frozen with tremorlabs/tremor now the copy-paste Raw components.

Cheap monthly re-scans: diff the awesome-dataviz Financial, Maps and Misc sections; count compatible-v2 in the Leaflet _plugins frontmatter; check the 'since' fields in ECharts chart-list-data.js; re-verify chartjs/awesome peerDependencies.
